actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

facts.text: The README starts model simulation with scripts/run_robot_sim.py
The project requires Python 3.8 or newer and is installed with pip install -e .
MujocoSimulator is the MuJoCo environment class that is independent from ROS
The simulator loads its scene with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path on the configured xml_path and creates mujoco.MjData from that model
The simulator overwrites the model's integration step with cfg.dt
MujocoSimulator.step runs cfg.decimation physics iterations; each iteration computes a torque, writes it to data.ctrl and calls mujoco.mj_step
The simulator computes its joint torque as target_trq + kp * (q_target - q) + kd * (dq_target - dq)
set_joint_commands converts q, dq, trq, kp and kd to flattened float32 arrays
The simulator reset zeroes qvel, optionally writes the base pose and joint positions, and calls mujoco.mj_forward
MujocoEnv wraps MujocoSimulator with a fixed-Hz stepping thread and DDS publishing to mimic hardware
When step_hz is omitted, MujocoEnv sets its period to max(1e-6, dt * max(1, decimation)); otherwise it uses the supplied step_hz
G1MujocoConfig selects deploy_robot/assets/mjcf/g1.xml as the scene and the pelvis as its root body
G1MujocoConfig uses decimation 10 and dt 0.002 s
G1_NUM_MOTOR is defined as 29
G1JointNames lists the 29 joint names in controller order from left_hip_pitch_joint to right_wrist_yaw_joint
The shipped simulation script builds MujocoEnv(G1MujocoConfig)
The model root element is '<mujoco model="g1">' and its compiler element declares angle radian and meshdir ../meshes/g1
The robot body is pelvis at 0 0 0.793 with a free joint named floating_base_joint
The actuator block declares one motor per actuated joint, named after the joint, and no motor element declares a ctrlrange
G1.__init__ calls ChannelFactoryInitialize in the real branch, but its function-local import and self.factory assignment occur in the sim branch

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates one model deterministically from one initial state, but this package offers no working seed: cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults and the seed input is recorded only.  The stand-in is deterministic too, yet its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the model for the joint dimensions, the actuator count, the actuator joint targets, the absent ctrlrange and the option timestep, then integrates a placeholder velocity proportional to each control value; it resolves no contact, friction, gravity, equality, tendon, actuator or free-base dynamics and loads no mesh, texture, sensor or camera

the upstream control layer is NOT COVERED: MujocoSimulator.step computes a PD torque from q, dq, trq, kp and kd joint commands and runs cfg.decimation (10) physics steps per control step (mujoco_simulator.py:275-283, :321-322, :339-346); the MuJoCo bridge writes data.ctrl directly and mj_step runs once per requested tick, so the PD law, the decimation and the controller-order joint remapping are not reproduced

the upstream MujocoEnv fixed-Hz thread and the DDS lowcmd/lowstate topic layer are not part of this driver (mujoco_env.py:15-24, :36-43); the bridge advances only on a step command, and there is no viewer, rendering or camera stream

the model declares no actuator ctrlrange (g1.xml:386-416), so the bridge publishes action.ctrl operator_required: a step that sets it is refused until the deployment's site-limits.json bounds it, and site-limits.example.json is operator example data, not a model bound

the model sets no <option timestep>, so the bridge uses the engine default; the deployed upstream simulator overwrites it with G1MujocoConfig.dt = 0.002 s (mujoco_simulator.py:82, config/g1.py:10) and the stand-in uses the same 0.002 s placeholder; the real engine was not run to confirm the value

MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine or with the upstream simulator, and the sim backend that imports mujoco was not run
no physical G1 robot is modelled or driven; the upstream real branch of the G1 robot is a hardware path this simulated package never opens

the excluded G1 real constructor is broken at the pin: ChannelFactoryInitialize is imported locally only in the sim branch but called first in the real branch, and self.factory is assigned only in sim (deploy_robot/g1/g1.py:58-69); the raw MJCF bridge does not instantiate this class

the fake resets to the MJCF pelvis pose (0, 0, 0.793) and identity free-joint quaternion, not the upstream wrapper's configured joint pose; it omits the full MuJoCo integration checkpoint API, uses mujoco_basic_v1, and declares snapshot_restore false for this backend

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

operator_required.name: step
operator_required.reason: the model gives none of its actuators no control range (ctrllimited false or no ctrlrange), so MuJoCo leaves the control unclamped; site-limits.json must bound action.ctrl before a step can set it

safe_state.description: bridge-owned lockstep integration stops; no step or world reset is accepted while latched. The integration state, velocities and controls are retained and readable. mhs.safety.reset only clears the latch; a new step is required and a step without action reuses retained controls
